findings.title: clamd port reachable from every cluster pod
findings.problem: The chart runs clamd as its own Deployment with `TCPAddr 0.0.0.0` behind a ClusterIP Service, and `networkPolicy.enabled` defaults to false (values.yaml:437). The README and the standalone clamd.conf/kubernetes.yaml describe clamd bound to 127.0.0.1 inside the validator pod, so the documented residual-risk claim does not hold for chart installs.
findings.impact: When hosted-apps is enabled with chart defaults, any workload in the cluster can reach clamd's unauthenticated port 3310 and send it SHUTDOWN/RELOAD or heavy INSTREAM scans. That takes the scanner down, so every upload fails validation, and the validator port is cluster-reachable as well.
findings.recommendation: Turn on the hosted-apps NetworkPolicies by default whenever `hosted-apps.enabled` is true, or render the clamd/validator policies unconditionally, so that only the validator pod can reach clamd:3310. Then align the README residual-risk text and kubernetes.yaml with the chart's separate-Deployment topology.
findings.check_notes: clamd-networkpolicy.yaml now renders whenever hosted-apps is enabled, admitting only validator pods to clamd; networkPolicy.enabled defaults true.

fix.change: Chart clamd NetworkPolicy (ingress from validator only) rendered whenever hosted-apps is enabled; networkPolicy.enabled defaults to true; kubernetes.yaml, clamd.conf and README realigned to the separate clamd Deployment

findings.title: Chart and runbook disagree on validator service names
findings.problem: The chart creates `codemie-hosted-apps-validator` / `codemie-hosted-apps-clamd` in the `codemie-hosted-apps` namespace. The README and kubernetes.yaml use `codemie-hosted-validator` / `codemie-hosted-clamd`, README section 3 documents `HOSTED_APPS_VALIDATOR_URL=http://codemie-hosted-validator:8091`, and the values.yaml comment suggests a short name that does not resolve across namespaces.
findings.impact: An operator following either document configures a validator URL that does not resolve, so validation is unavailable and no hosted app can be published. Reachability was not confirmed against a rendered chart.
findings.recommendation: Use one set of names across the chart, README and kubernetes.yaml. In the values.yaml and README examples, document the namespace-qualified validator URL (`http://codemie-hosted-apps-validator.<hosted namespace>.svc:8091`).
findings.check_notes: Chart, README, kubernetes.yaml and values.yaml use codemie-hosted-apps-validator with the namespace-qualified .svc URL.

fix.change: One set of names (codemie-hosted-apps-validator/-clamd) across chart, kubernetes.yaml and README; namespace-qualified validator URL in values.yaml and README

findings.title: New modules omit future annotations import
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types and Imports) says to add `from __future__ import annotations` in new modules. 45 new src/codemie modules omit it, for example service/hosted_applications/catalog.py, worker.py, rest_api/routers/hosted_applications.py, hosted_apps_validator/server.py and core/hosted_applications/settings.py.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard is unmet across most of the new package surface, and no Ruff rule (FA) enforces it.
findings.recommendation: Add `from __future__ import annotations` after the license header in each new src/codemie module that lacks it.
findings.check_notes: All 68 added src/codemie modules carry from __future__ import annotations.

fix.change: Added `from __future__ import annotations` to the 45 new src/codemie modules that lacked it

findings.title: Revocation SID taken from unverified header token
findings.problem: For platform_jwt providers (keycloak, oidc, entraid-oidc without the JWKS wrapper), record_platform_identity decodes the token from `x-auth-request-access-token` / Authorization with `verify_signature: False` and uses its sid, iat and auth_time for the hosted identity and SID-based revocation. The enterprise IdP that actually authenticated the request is not in this repository, so I could not confirm it reads the same header.
findings.impact: If the platform authenticates from a different header or cookie, a signed-in caller who controls this header can choose their own sid/iat and escape SID-based revocation or the logout cutoff. Reachability was not confirmed because the enterprise IdP code is outside this repository.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether platform_jwt providers may feed SID-based revocation. If they may, bind the hosted identity to the token the enterprise IdP actually verified, for example by having keycloak/oidc providers store their verified claims on request.state the way JwksValidatingIdp does. Otherwise do not use `sid` from an unverified token for revocation decisions.
findings.check_notes: Decision recorded (no claims from unverified token); bind_forwarded_identity binds platform_jwt by digest with sid/auth_time None; tests updated.

fix.change: platform_jwt binds through new bind_forwarded_identity: no sid/iat/auth_time/exp from the unverified token, digest binding, issued_at = acceptance time; bind_identity is verified-claims only; README 5 and spec 8/11 updated

decision.outcome: platform_jwt providers must NOT feed SID-based revocation or any hosted identity claim from an unverified token: take sid/iat/auth_time only from verified claims (local_jwt, jwks); for platform_jwt, bind the hosted identity without SID (sessions bounded by token lifetime and the existing principal-level revocation on platform logout); update spec 8 identity / 11 security and hosted-applications/README.md 5; add tests.
decision.rationale: The forwarded token is decoded without signature verification, so any claim in it could be chosen by a caller who controls the header; binding by the token digest with issued_at at platform acceptance and relying on the sid-less per-principal logout cutoff removes that lever while keeping the platform_jwt trust model.

findings.title: Cross-app cookie bombing locks viewers out
findings.problem: Every app version is served from a subdomain of one registrable content domain, so uploaded JS on any app can set many `Domain=<content domain>` cookies. parse_session_cookies raises ValueError as soon as the Cookie header exceeds COOKIE_HEADER_LIMIT (8192).
findings.impact: Any internal user who uploads an app can make every viewer who opens it get 401 on all hosted apps until they clear their cookies. This is a cross-tenant availability attack.
findings.recommendation: Do not fail the whole request on an oversized Cookie header. Instead, parse only the platform session cookie names and ignore the rest, or have the gateway strip non-session cookies set on the parent content domain. Add a test with a Cookie header larger than 8 KiB that includes a valid session cookie.
findings.check_notes: parse_session_cookies no longer limits header length; non-platform cookie pairs are ignored; COOKIE_HEADER_LIMIT removed.

fix.change: parse_session_cookies no longer refuses a long Cookie header; it reads only the platform names

findings.title: Lossy ASCII encoding in host dispatch matcher
findings.problem: security-patterns.md forbids lossy normalization before a security decision. HostDispatcher builds `_domain_bytes` with `domain.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")`, and `_mentions_content` uses it to decide whether a non-canonical Host goes to content or management. HostedSettings.from_config does not reject a non-ASCII content domain outright.
findings.impact: With a non-ASCII configured content domain, the substring check stops matching, so malformed content hosts route to management instead of failing closed. The trigger is operator configuration; reachability was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Encode strictly with `domain.encode("ascii")` and raise ValueError at construction for a non-ASCII content domain, the same way an empty domain is already rejected.
findings.check_notes: HostDispatcher encodes the content domain strictly and raises ValueError for non-ASCII.

fix.change: HostDispatcher encodes the content domain strictly and raises ValueError for a non-ASCII domain

findings.title: clamd signature date assumed UTC
findings.problem: parse_scanner_version parses clamd's signature date with strptime and then `.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`, but clamd formats that date in its own local time.
findings.impact: A clamd container whose TZ is ahead of UTC makes every signature date look as if it is in the future, which trips the 5-minute future check, so every scan is refused and validation becomes unavailable. A TZ behind UTC shifts the 48-hour staleness window. Reachability depends on the container's TZ and was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Either pin TZ=UTC on the clamd container (chart, kubernetes.yaml, Dockerfile) and document that the parser relies on it, or interpret the stamp in the scanner's timezone before the staleness and future checks.
findings.check_notes: Chart clamd.env and kubernetes.yaml pin TZ=UTC; parser comment and README document the reliance.

fix.change: TZ=UTC pinned on the clamd container in values.yaml, chart README and kubernetes.yaml; parser reliance documented in scanner.py and README 7

findings.title: Parser stderr pipe can deadlock validation
findings.problem: Inspector.parser pipes both stdout and stderr from the sandbox subprocess but reads stderr only after stdout reaches EOF and process.wait() returns. A parser that writes more than a pipe buffer (~64 KiB) to stderr, such as a long traceback or per-file warnings caused by a crafted upload, blocks on that write.
findings.impact: The child never closes stdout, so the validation job hangs until its budget timeout and fails with 503. While it hangs it holds a validator slot, and a crafted upload can trigger this on every retry. Reachability depends on how much the sandbox writes to stderr and was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Drain stderr while stdout is being read, for example `stderr_task = asyncio.create_task(process.stderr.read(64 * 1024))` started before the stdout loop and awaited after `process.wait()`. Discard anything past the bound so the child never blocks on a full stderr pipe.
findings.check_notes: stderr drained concurrently via a bounded _drain task started before reading stdout.

fix.change: Inspector.parser drains stderr in a task while stdout is read, keeping the first 64 KiB

findings.title: Failed put leaves partial immutable object
findings.problem: PrefixWriter.put creates the object with O_EXCL and increments used_objects/used_bytes. Only the digest-mismatch branch unlinks the object and refunds the counters. An oversize chunk, a non-bytes chunk (which raises an untyped ValueError) or a final size mismatch leaves the partial file on disk.
findings.impact: A retry that writes the same key hits FileExistsError, which returns 409 STORAGE_IMMUTABLE, and the reservation counters stay inflated. Whether retries reuse the key was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: On every failure after `_create_object` succeeds (oversize chunk, non-bytes chunk, size mismatch, OSError), unlink the partial object and refund `used_objects`/`used_bytes`, as the digest-mismatch branch already does. Raise a typed HostedApplicationError instead of a bare `ValueError("Invalid storage chunk")`.
findings.check_notes: put() discards the partial object and refunds counters on any failure in _write; non-bytes chunks raise typed HostedApplicationError.

fix.change: PrefixWriter.put unlinks the partial object and refunds counters on every failure after creation; non-bytes chunk raises typed STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE

findings.title: PATCH description null escapes validation
findings.problem: AppPatch makes `description: StrictStr | None` but inherits AppCreate.description_text, which calls `unicodedata.normalize("NFC", value)` without checking for None. A PATCH body with `"description": null` raises TypeError inside the field validator. Pydantic converts only ValueError and AssertionError, so the TypeError is not turned into a validation error, and the has_changes check never runs.
findings.impact: A client error becomes a 5xx (503 through HostedAPIRoute) instead of 422 on a public endpoint. That misleads clients and monitoring.
findings.recommendation: In `description_text`, reject non-strings first with `if not isinstance(value, str): raise ValueError("Description is required")`, the same way `_plain` does, so that AppPatch answers 422.
findings.check_notes: description_text rejects non-strings with ValueError before NFC normalization, so PATCH null gives 422.

fix.change: AppCreate.description_text rejects a non-string with ValueError so AppPatch answers 422

findings.title: Untyped public helpers in hosted API layer
findings.problem: code-quality.md forbids untyped public functions in new code. runtime(), mutation(), reply(), unavailable_capabilities() in the router, and verified_context(), require_verified_context(), hosted_identity(), guard_mutation() in rest_api/security/hosted_applications.py, leave parameters or return types unannotated. Route handlers also declare their dependencies as untyped `identity=Depends(...)` / `value=Depends(...)`.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard is broken in new public API-layer code, and the Ruff gate does not enforce ANN rules.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the parameters and return types of runtime(), mutation(), reply(), unavailable_capabilities(), verified_context(), require_verified_context(), hosted_identity() and guard_mutation(). Type the handler dependencies as HostedActor/HostedApplicationsRuntime, as open_share_link and get_share_link already do.
findings.check_notes: runtime, mutation, reply, unavailable_capabilities and the security helpers are fully annotated; dependencies typed.

fix.change: Annotated runtime, mutation, reply, unavailable_capabilities, verified_context, require_verified_context, hosted_identity, guard_mutation and every hosted route handler's dependencies and return type

findings.title: Suspend no-op skips administrator actor_kind
findings.problem: Spec 5.6 requires moderation operations to be recorded with actor_kind='administrator'. When an already-suspended app is suspended again, security() returns through tx.finish before `op.actor_kind = "administrator"` is set, so the operation keeps the default 'user'. _reinstate also passes `Actor(user.id, "user")` to retire_version, although spec 8 says reinstate retires the version as the admin.
findings.impact: The audit trail attributes an administrator takedown, or a version retirement during reinstate, to an ordinary user. This is a spec requirement that is only partly met.
findings.recommendation: Set `op.actor_kind = "administrator"` right after the replay check, before the suspended-twice early return. In `_reinstate`, pass `Actor(user.id, "administrator")` to `retire_version` so that the retirement is attributed to the admin, as spec 8 requires.
findings.check_notes: actor_kind='administrator' set right after replay check, before no-op suspend return; reinstate retires as administrator.

fix.change: op.actor_kind = 'administrator' set right after the replay check; reinstate retires the previous version as Actor(user.id, 'administrator')

findings.title: Unchanged shared=true blocks edits when suspended
findings.problem: patch_app calls `suspend_refuses(app, "share_on")` whenever `request.shared is True`, even when the app is already shared. Moves are compared with the current project, but share_on is not compared with the current value.
findings.impact: A metadata edit, such as a name change, on a suspended shared app that re-sends the unchanged `shared=true` (as a full-form client does) is refused with 409 APP_SUSPENDED, although the spec gates only a real share-on transition.
findings.recommendation: Gate only a real share-on transition: `if request.shared is True and not app.shared: suspend_refuses(app, "share_on")`.
findings.check_notes: share_on suspension check gated on a real transition (shared True and not app.shared).

fix.change: patch_app gates share_on only when the app is not already shared

findings.title: lock_timeout is not the first open statement
findings.problem: Spec 6.3 step 1 requires `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '400ms'` as the first statement of the share-link open transaction. open_share_link sets it first in its own body, but repository.transaction(write=True) has already run `SELECT clock_timestamp()` and the _check_sign_in reads.
findings.impact: The code deviates from the spec as written. Those earlier reads take no row locks, so lock waits stay bounded today, but a later lock added to _check_sign_in would silently escape the 400 ms bound.
findings.recommendation: Decide between two fixes. Either move `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` into `repository.transaction` (an option used by open_share_link) so it runs before the `clock_timestamp()` and `_check_sign_in` reads, or amend spec 6.3 step 1 to say the timeout must come before the first locking statement. The current reads take no row locks.
findings.check_notes: Decision recorded; transaction(lock_timeout_ms=...) issues SET LOCAL lock_timeout before clock_timestamp and sign-in reads; open_share_link passes it.

fix.change: repository.transaction(lock_timeout_ms=) runs SET LOCAL lock_timeout as its first statement; open_share_link passes SHARE_LINK_OPEN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS

decision.outcome: Move SET LOCAL lock_timeout into repository.transaction as an option used by open_share_link so it is the first statement of that transaction, before clock_timestamp() and the sign-in reads; keep spec 6.3 as written.
decision.rationale: Making the timeout the transaction's first statement satisfies spec 6.3 step 1 literally and keeps any lock later added to the sign-in checks inside the 400 ms bound.

findings.title: Owner can grant access to themselves
findings.problem: _prepare_grant runs the owner check and de-duplication, but nothing removes the owner's own id from user_ids. The owner passes the recipient check, so a self-grant row is upserted.
findings.impact: The owner appears in shared_with, and the 'people' sharing filter classifies a private app as shared with people. That misleads both the owner and the catalog filters.
findings.recommendation: Remove the owner's own id in `_prepare_grant`, for example with `ids = [uid for uid in _dedupe(user_ids) if uid != owner.id]`, or refuse it with a 400, so that no self-grant row is written.
findings.check_notes: _prepare_grant drops the owner's own id after dedupe, so no self-grant row is written.

fix.change: _prepare_grant drops the owner's own id after de-duplication

findings.title: Commit subject breaks ticket-prefix format
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires the commit subject format `EPMCDME-####: Description`. In f2900a55..HEAD, the commit `epmcdme-16173: add planning artifacts` uses a lowercase ticket prefix and a lowercase description.
findings.impact: This breaks a documented repository convention, and the guide also requires the final squash commit to keep the ticket-prefixed format.
findings.recommendation: Reword the subject to `EPMCDME-16173: Add planning artifacts`, or make sure the squash-merge commit message uses the documented format.
findings.check_notes: Commit reworded to 'EPMCDME-16173: Add planning artifacts' (1759ba8af); all 127 subjects in origin/main..HEAD match the format.

decision.outcome: Reword commit 17cb43f3a to 'EPMCDME-16173: Add planning artifacts' (now 1759ba8af) by rebasing the branch chain with --update-refs; trees of all three branches are byte-identical to before.
decision.rationale: User chose to reword the commit so no non-conforming subject remains in origin/main..HEAD.

disposition.rationale: Not fixed by design: commit 17cb43f3a belongs to the original author's branch history, and the MR is merged with a squash commit whose message follows the "EPMCDME-15659: <subject>" format, so the lowercase subject never reaches main. Rewriting it would rebase the whole branch chain for no effect on the merged result.

Two decision_needed items remain (CR-004 unverified-token SID for revocation, CR-014 spec 6.3 lock_timeout ordering) alongside a clamd exposure (CR-001), an audit actor_kind gap (CR-012, spec 5.6 partial) and standards partials; 0 deferred, 35 dismissed as noise, spec-mandated design, or unreachable.
